title: Only 12% Pass This Chef's Entrance Exam
summary: Test your kitchen instincts with tools, ingredients, cooking methods and practical decisions.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
Move from familiar kitchen tools to ingredients, baking, recipe calculations and practical cooking decisions. Each set tests a different part of kitchen knowledge.

Choose one answer, see your topic profile at the checkpoint and continue to a fresh challenge. Reveal your overall score and optionally review missed answers at the end.

Measurements state their units explicitly. Food-safety questions use broad principles rather than country-specific rules. Your result describes this quiz attempt and is not a practical cooking assessment.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This quiz is not a culinary qualification, professional kitchen assessment or food-safety certification. Always follow local food-safety requirements and qualified guidance.

chef-s1q1.question: Which tool is designed to grip and turn hot pieces of food?

chef-s1q2.question: Which tool is best suited to beating air into cream by hand?

chef-s1q3.question: Which tool drains water from cooked pasta?

chef-s1q4.question: Which tool removes a thin layer of skin from a carrot?

chef-s1q5.question: Which tool is used to roll dough into a flat sheet?

chef-s1q6.question: Which tool measures the mass of flour most directly?

chef-s2q1.question: A recipe is ready. What makes the cooking steps easier to follow?

answers.a1: Skip the timings until the end

chef-s2q2.question: Why cut vegetables into similar-sized pieces for the same pan?

answers.a1: They cook at a more similar rate
answers.a4: They all develop the same taste

chef-s2q3.question: What does it mean to zest a lemon?

answers.a1: Remove the thin outer coloured layer
answers.a4: Cut the whole lemon into slices

chef-s2q4.question: Which preparation gives garlic a finer texture?

chef-s2q5.question: Why dry washed leaves before dressing a salad?

answers.a2: So the leaves need no washing next time
answers.a3: So excess water does not dilute the dressing

chef-s2q6.question: A recipe needs sliced onion first and fresh herbs last. How should they be prepared?

answers.a1: Cook the herbs before slicing the onion
answers.a2: Mix them together and add both first
answers.a3: Keep them separate for their different timings

chef-s2q7.question: What does “fold in” usually ask you to do?

chef-s3q1.question: Which method cooks food in water vapour above hot water?

chef-s3q2.question: Which method surrounds food with hot, dry oven air?

chef-s3q3.question: Which method uses gentle liquid heat below a vigorous boil?

chef-s3q4.question: Which surface best describes a gentle simmer?

chef-s3q5.question: A crowded pan of vegetables becomes wet instead of browning. Why?

answers.a1: Released moisture is trapped and steaming the food
answers.a4: The pan is producing extra salt

chef-s3q6.question: Braising usually combines browning with which next step?

answers.a3: Gentle cooking with some liquid in a covered pot

chef-s3q7.question: Why can a rolling boil damage delicate pieces of fish?

answers.a1: It turns the bones into steam
answers.a2: Strong movement can break them apart
answers.a4: It makes water stop transferring heat

chef-s4q1.question: A rich sauce tastes heavy. Which small addition can add acidity?

chef-s4q2.question: Which ingredient is strongly associated with savoury umami taste?

chef-s4q4.question: A sauce is too salty. Which addition can dilute the salt concentration?

chef-s4q5.question: Why are delicate fresh herbs often added near the end of cooking?

answers.a1: To turn them into a thickener
answers.a2: To make them absorb all the salt
answers.a3: To stop the dish containing water
answers.a4: To retain more of their fresh aroma

chef-s4q6.question: Which ingredient contributes acidity to a basic vinaigrette?

chef-s4q7.question: Which tasting approach best controls seasoning?

answers.a1: Taste only before any ingredients are mixed
answers.a2: Add a little, mix, then taste again
answers.a3: Season only by the colour of the pan
answers.a4: Add the full salt supply at once

chef-s5q1.question: What happens when a sauce is reduced by simmering?

answers.a2: Water evaporates and flavours become more concentrated

chef-s5q2.question: What is an emulsion in cooking?

answers.a2: A layer of ice on a sauce
answers.a3: A dry mixture of whole spices
answers.a4: One liquid dispersed as droplets in another

chef-s5q3.question: Which pair of liquids forms the basis of a simple vinaigrette?

chef-s5q4.question: What is a roux usually made from?

chef-s5q5.question: Why mix starch with a little cold liquid before adding it to a hot sauce?

answers.a4: To help disperse it and reduce lumps

chef-s5q6.question: What does deglazing a pan help collect?

answers.a1: The raw flour still in its bag
answers.a2: The browned bits stuck to the pan
answers.a3: The moisture inside a closed jar
answers.a4: Only the steam above the pan

chef-s5q7.question: A sauce needs a smooth finish without solid pieces. Which method fits?

answers.a4: Pass it through a fine sieve

chef-s6q1.question: Which ingredient produces gas as it ferments in bread dough?

chef-s6q2.question: Why can mixing wheat-flour muffin batter too much make it tough?

chef-s6q3.question: Why keep pieces of butter cold when making flaky pastry?

answers.a1: They help create separate layers during baking
answers.a4: They dissolve all the flour immediately

chef-s6q4.question: Which ingredient helps an egg custard set as it heats?

chef-s6q5.question: What does kneading wheat bread dough mainly help develop?

answers.a3: Baking a pastry case before adding its filling

chef-s6q7.question: A bread dough grows during its warm resting period. What is happening?

answers.a2: The flour is turning into salt
answers.a4: The bowl is creating extra dough

chef-s7q1.question: A recipe uses 300 g of rice for 4 portions. How much for 10 equal portions?

chef-s7q2.question: You need 3 portions of 175 g each. What is the total mass?

chef-s7q3.question: Divide 1.5 L equally between 3 containers. How much goes in each?

chef-s7q4.question: Flour and sugar are mixed in a 2:1 ratio by mass. For 600 g flour, how much sugar?

chef-s7q5.question: A recipe needs 240 g of butter. You are making half. How much is needed?

chef-s7q6.question: A dish goes into the oven at 14:10 for 25 minutes. When is that time up?

chef-s7q7.question: You have 2 kg of dough. Each portion uses 125 g. How many full portions?

chef-s8q1.question: Raw chicken and ready-to-eat salad need preparation. Which setup reduces contamination?

answers.a1: The raw chicken placed over the salad
answers.a2: Separate clean equipment for the salad
answers.a3: A shared cloth to wipe both foods
answers.a4: The same unwashed board for both

chef-s8q2.question: What should happen before preparing food after handling waste?

answers.a1: Continue if the waste looked clean

chef-s8q3.question: Why keep raw and cooked foods separate?

answers.a1: To make all food taste the same
answers.a2: To reduce transfer of harmful microorganisms
answers.a3: To prevent cooked food losing its colour

chef-s8q4.question: Which water should be used to wash produce eaten raw?

answers.a1: Any water if it looks clear
answers.a3: Water used to rinse raw meat
answers.a4: Water that is safe to drink

chef-s8q5.question: Which tool measures a food’s internal temperature?

chef-s8q6.question: A guest reports a food allergy. What is the best general approach?

answers.a1: Check ingredients and prevent allergen cross-contact
answers.a4: Remove only visible pieces after cooking

chef-s8q7.question: Why can a used utensil transfer an allergen into another dish?

answers.a3: Small residues can remain on it
answers.a4: Allergens disappear when food is mixed

chef-s9q1.question: One component takes 20 minutes and another takes 5. To finish together, start which first?

answers.a2: Neither until the other is ready

chef-s9q2.question: A recipe says to rest dough for 30 minutes before rolling. What belongs in the plan?

answers.a2: The resting time as well as active preparation

chef-s9q3.question: A sauce must simmer while vegetables roast. What helps avoid missing either task?

answers.a2: One timer with no task label

chef-s9q4.question: Six plates need two identical pieces each. How many pieces should be ready?

chef-s9q5.question: A recipe lists onions before garlic in the pan. Which approach follows it?

answers.a2: Add the onions first, then the garlic at the stated step
answers.a4: Add the garlic only after serving

chef-s9q6.question: A dish needs a crisp topping at service. When is the topping best added?

answers.a1: Before a long soak in the sauce
answers.a2: Close to serving so it stays crisp
answers.a4: While the ingredients are being washed

chef-s9q7.question: A plate looks unfinished. What is the purpose of a suitable edible garnish?

answers.a1: Make every portion heavier than planned
answers.a2: Support the dish’s appearance and taste

chef-s10q1.question: Vegetables need browning but steam in a crowded pan. Which change addresses the cause?

answers.a3: Add more water and cover tightly

chef-s10q2.question: A reduced sauce is too strong and thick. What can help restore balance?

answers.a2: Add a little suitable unsalted liquid and taste

chef-s10q3.question: A recipe for 12 equal portions uses 1,800 g of an ingredient. How much for 18?

chef-s10q4.question: A pastry recipe requires 200 g flour and 100 g butter. You used 200 g of each. What changed?

chef-s10q5.question: A soup is boiling hard and losing liquid too quickly. What addresses both issues?

answers.a1: Use a wider pan on maximum heat
answers.a3: Continue until the pan is dry
answers.a4: Lower the heat to a gentle simmer

chef-s10q6.question: One task takes 12 minutes and must finish before a 6-minute task starts. What is the minimum total?

chef-s10q7.question: An oil-and-vinegar dressing separates after standing. What best explains it?

answers.a1: The oil has turned into water
answers.a2: The bowl has removed all the acidity
answers.a3: The vinegar has become solid salt
answers.a4: The liquids are not held in a stable emulsion
